newsitem.title: RUSSIA: German abducted near Russia's Chechnya region.
newsitem.headline: German abducted near Russia's Chechnya region.

text.p: A German businessman has been abducted near Russia's breakaway republic of Chechnya, the latest victim of a string of kidnappings there, Russia's NTV said on Saturday.
The foreign ministry in Bonn confirmed the man was seized a few days ago and said its embassy was in contact with Russian authorities about the case.
NTV said the German was seized along with a Yugoslav man accompanying him at the airport of Nazran, capital of the neighbouring Ingushetia region, from where they were planning to fly to Chechnya.
It said the German wanted to organise a delivery of medical supplies to the north Caucasus region.
Chechnya is still struggling to recover from 21 months of fighting between Russian troops and separatist forces which ended a year ago. Russian troops completed their withdrawal early this year.
Few details were available on the kidnapping, part of a wave of abductions in the unruly region. Six Russian journalists, two Britons, a Frenchman and a Slovak man are still missing.
Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov on Thursday offered amnesty to hostage takers on condition that they release their victims by August 10 -- or face the death penalty or life imprisonment.
Five Russian soldiers have been freed this week in Chechnya, which has been seeking to improve its image and attract desperately needed funds to rebuild its shattered economy.

President Boris Yeltsin agreed on Friday during a telephone conversation with Maskhadov to meet him soon in Moscow to discuss relations -- with an emphasis on the need to restore the rule of law, the Kremlin said.
Moscow and Chechnya's separatist leaders agreed a truce last August after fighting which killed tens of thousands of people.

But the peace process has been hampered by disagreement over the republic's status, which has been left to be determined at a future date. Maskhadov says it is independent and Yeltsin insists it is and must remain part of the Russian Federation.
